div.p: May I revert today to the matter of my protégé, Fritz M. Rabinovitsch about which I have told you repeatedly. He is an especially intelligent young man of great integrity who has excellent prospects in whatever academic career he may choose.

In 1935, aged 22, he was arrested on the grounds that he had belonged to a group of young people reputedly hostile to the State, and of having helped a friend to escape from Germany . For that he was sentenced to two years of hard labor. I talked to the counsel who defended him at the time, who fully confirmed my impression that young Rabinovitsch is a man of admirable character.

Already while he served his term in prison I was assembling documents in support of an immigration visa for him and the opinion of the Consul was encouraging in case the boy could apply for the visa in person.

When the boy’s term had expired he was not discharged but taken to a concentration camp, where he has now been for more than a year. The real reason for detaining the young man seems to be, on the one hand, the fact that he is loyal and courageous and, in spite of the terrible pressure exerted upon him, has not been converted to National Socialism, and on the other hand, the fear that he could spread more information on conditions in German prisons and concentration camps. As far as I know, the boy had to stay in a hospital for months as a result of the tortures he suffered.

In spite of all that I have not given up my efforts to have the boy set free and make his immigration to the United States possible. I just heard from the German counsel that there is a certain chance of the boy’s being discharged of he can produce a few letters from noted American personalities to the effect that they take personal interest in him. The German authorities claim that the boy used to be a Communist (which is not true) and fear that in America he would associate with
Anti-fascist and Communist circles; so these letters should mainly express that in America the boy will devote himself to his further academic training and not to any political activity.

I told you already that arrangements have been made in order to enable the boy to study at New York University immediately upon his arrival. He is admitted to the School of Commerce there. The expenses of his training will be met. I should be very grateful if you would succeed in finding a personality well known in America who would express his conviction [?] boy is talented and that his moral standard is high, his interest in him, and his readiness to supervise the boy’s academic training in the case of his immigration and to exercise his influence over him. The letter or letters will be submitted by the German counsel both to the German authorities to obtain the discharge, and to the American Consul for his informationally (evtl. unleserlich) counsel’s opinion is that possibly the boy’s freeing and [?] of his life which is in danger at present may depend upon the quality of the personalities and the warmth of their interest. He thinks that on the whole the chances are not bad. Naturally this mater is very urgent, for any day now events may occur and make the situation worse.

My own name, being that of an emigré Jewish professor, must not be mentioned; so the letters should not be addressed to me, but to Dr. Philip C. Jessup , 15 William Street, New York City . Dr. Jessup , being a lawyer, is himself charged with the case over here. Dr. Jessup asked me to see that, if all possible, the letters reach him on Tuesday morning at the latest so that they can be sent over by the “Queen Mary”. I thank you in advance for anything you may be able to do in the matter. I personally guarantee that the boy will never discredit you.
